newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium ends little changed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium ends little changed in dull trade.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures ended little changed on Wednesday in dull trade, reflecting minor movements in the foreign exchange market, traders said.
Prices were down 0.5 yen to up 0.1 yen, with the benchmark February 1998 contract adding 0.1 yen to 205.2 yen per kg.
The day's volume was 3,460 lots, down from the 3,890 lots on Tuesday but above a low of 2,517 on Monday.

"Nobody is willing to move the metal's price in Tokyo. The fluctuations purely reflect London prices and movements in the foreign exchange market," said a trader. "Liquidity is so low. You can't take positions you like. Even people who were in the
market at the beginning are now sidelined and watching."
Asked about prices in London, one trader said: "It should not go down very much further. But we should be prepared to see US$1,530 (a tonne) as we hear Midwest premiums are falling."
Aluminium closed in the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday at $1,555 a tonne.
The trader added premiums in Tokyo were also under pressure, with some deals made with a premium of $75 per tonne over LME cash prices, compared with $82-$87 last week.
